title: GLOBE · COMMAND & ALERT
text:
GLOBE · COMMAND & ALERT
The globe shows bases, radar outposts, detected UFOs, crash sites, aircraft, and satellite coverage. The left command menu opens the other screens. ALERT reports current threat; click it to open the contact list. Time controls are in the top bar.BASE / LOCATIONSCreate a base from BASE. Rent space centers under LOCATIONS; their facilities and launch sites become available only while leased.TIME & ALERTPause or advance the simulation from the top row. UFO detection messages appear when a radar or satellite actually detects a contact.

title: BASE · CONSTRUCTION & FACILITIES
text:
BASE · CONSTRUCTION & FACILITIES
Select a base on the globe to open its base screen. The grid shows occupied and available cells; choose a structure from the right construction panel and place it on a free area.BUILDINGSChoose a building on the right to see its cost, size, and placement preview. Click a valid grid location to build.STAFF & CAPACITYBuild housing, hospital, training, and work facilities to support soldiers and staff. Crew and facility controls are shown in their corresponding sections.

title: AIRCRAFT · HANGAR & MISSIONS
text:
AIRCRAFT · HANGAR & MISSIONS
Choose an aircraft in the selector. Its status, crew, fuel, ammunition, damage, and service state appear in the hangar.CREWHire people in WORKFORCE, then assign pilots, navigators, and technicians in the aircraft crew panel.SERVICEUse SERVICE AIRCRAFT to repair damage and replenish fuel and ammunition. These operations cost money and game time.MISSIONSLaunch an aircraft from the base/aircraft controls. Interceptors must have enough range to reach the target and return.

title: SOLDIERS · ROSTER & EQUIPMENT
text:
SOLDIERS · ROSTER & EQUIPMENT
The roster lists available candidates and hired soldiers. Select a soldier to open the profile, then choose EQUIP SOLDIER to manage their loadout.PROFILERename the soldier in the profile. The profile shows rank, role, health, attributes, and the agility radar.EQUIPMENTClick a weapon, armor, medical, backpack, belt, or belt-content slot to choose an available item from storage. Starter roles are scout, sniper, tank, and medic.MEDICThe starter medic carries basic AID. Medics can train in the base hospital when one is available.

title: STORAGE · INVENTORY & TRADE
text:
STORAGE · INVENTORY & TRADE
The left list groups weapons, ammunition, grenades, armor, aircraft parts, vehicles, and materials. Select an item to see its illustration, description, quantity, dimensions, storage volume, and prices on the right.BUY / SELLSet a quantity with the slider and choose BUY or SELL. Orders go through a national auction and cargo flight. Purchases are charged up front; goods are added only on arrival and only up to free storage capacity. Sale proceeds arrive with the cargo plane.WAREHOUSE LOADThe capacity display at the top shows occupied pallet space. Radioactive items carry the radiation symbol.

title: WORKFORCE · HIRING & TRAINING
text:
WORKFORCE · HIRING & TRAINING
Hire technicians, scientists, pilots, navigators, and other personnel here. The market refreshes weekly. Hire candidates from the appropriate role tab.AIRCRAFT CREWAssign hired pilots, navigators, and technicians in AIRCRAFT.SOLDIERSHire soldiers from the SOLDIERS screen. A soldier's role comes from their specialization; the four initial soldiers have fixed starter roles.

title: RESEARCH & MANUFACTURE
text:
RESEARCH & MANUFACTURE
RESEARCH is where scientists work on discovered technology. MANUFACTURE is where available designs can be produced from stored materials and components.RESEARCH STAFFHire scientists in WORKFORCE, then assign them to research projects.RESOURCESCheck recipes and material stock in STORAGE before starting production. Research unlocks advanced equipment and engine variants.

title: SPACE CENTERS · WHERE TO START
text:
SPACE CENTERS · WHERE TO START

A control center manages missions. A launch ramp is the place where you prepare and send a rocket. All durations below use game time: pausing stops the countdown, and fast-forward also advances payments, flights and supply consumption.

Open LOCATIONS in the left menu.
Choose the complex you need and check its rental price before paying.
Open its control center, then use its ramp button to prepare a flight. The arrow beside GLOBE collapses the complete left panel; click it again to reopen it.
HOUSTON FLIGHT CONTROL · NASA$400,000 per 30 game days. Controls ISS access and astronaut recruitment; FLORIDA LAUNCH RAMP opens the crewed launch site. Renting Houston does not pay for the ISS.ESA SPACE CENTER$400,000 per 30 game days. Monitors satellites. Use its Kourou ramp button to buy and launch satellites. The ramp's return button takes you back to ESA control.ROSCOSMOS SPACE CENTER$300,000 per 30 game days. Controls cargo missions from Baikonur. An active Roscosmos lease is needed when choosing Baikonur for automatic ISS supplies.AUTOMATIC CENTER RENEWALEvery 30 game days the game charges the center rental again. If funds are insufficient, access ends. Losing Houston also ends the ISS lease and its supply plan, even if the ISS had time prepaid. Keep a cash reserve before advancing time.

First ISS visit: rent HOUSTON FLIGHT CONTROL → choose an ISS term under OPEN ISS → pay RENT ISS → open ISS. First satellite: rent ESA → open Kourou → choose launch settings and satellite type → pay to schedule the rocket.

title: ROCKETS · PREPARE, PAY AND FOLLOW THE FLIGHT
text:
ROCKETS · PREPARE, PAY AND FOLLOW THE FLIGHT

The 3D model is a visual view of the launcher. Drag to rotate it, use the wheel or + / − to zoom, and RESET to restore its camera. Use the mission controls to schedule a launch.

ESA / KOUROU · SATELLITES
Open ESA, then its Kourou launch ramp. The displayed heavy launcher is Ariane 64.
Choose the number of rockets, from 1 to 5. Each carries one satellite. Choose the fuel setting and read the resulting altitude, scan coverage, scan detail and price.
Select the satellite's scan type using its SCHEDULE UNCREWED SATELLITE button. The complete order is charged immediately.
Read the queue in the right panel from top to bottom. Each row identifies the satellite payload and rocket number. LOADING is loading cargo; ROCKET PREPARATION is preparing the launcher; WAITING IN QUEUE means an earlier rocket goes first.
After launch, return to ESA to inspect the satellite fleet and its land, water and air scan counts. Check remaining satellite fuel and any low-fuel warning.

A normal queued rocket takes 12 game hours to load and 24 hours to prepare: 36 hours before launch, plus any delay. A higher altitude changes scan coverage and detail; compare the displayed values before paying. A satellite in the launch queue is not yet an active satellite in orbit.

FLORIDA · ASTRONAUTS AND GENERAL CARGO
Hire astronauts in Houston with HIRE. Residential cells provide their accommodation; one cell supports four astronauts. Their salary is a recurring monthly expense.
Open FLORIDA LAUNCH RAMP and assign at least one commander, one navigator and one technician. Researchers are optional. The flight crew selector supports up to eight people, but the ISS itself holds only seven: check BOARD CAPACITY before assigning passengers.
Choose cargo size and review the cost breakdown. The game calculates the corresponding fuel and ISS destination altitude.
Use SCHEDULE CREWED FLIGHT. One flight is scheduled and paid for. After its launch preparation, travel to ISS takes another 18 game hours. Crew and general cargo are registered on arrival, not when you pay.

General cargo is separate from automatic life-support supplies. Scheduling a crewed flight alone does not refill the oxygen, water and food graphs. Baikonur also supports uncrewed cargo operations through Roscosmos; review its cargo controls and price before scheduling.

WHY CAN'T I LAUNCH?
Check the complex lease, available money and required crew. A day reserved for ISS resupply blocks other rocket launches; a queued non-cargo rocket due on that day is postponed. Bad weather can delay automatic ISS supply launches. If the queue does not advance, check whether game time is paused. Use RETURN TO HOUSTON or RETURN TO ESA CONTROL to get back from the corresponding ramp.

title: ISS · RENTAL, PEOPLE AND SURVIVAL
text:
ISS · RENTAL, PEOPLE AND SURVIVAL

ISS means International Space Station. In this game it is an orbital outpost with a crew, limited supplies, solar power and fuel for maintaining its orbit. The 3D station shows its structure; the status cards above it show what needs your attention. These are game rules, not a real-world operating manual.

PAYING FOR ACCESS
First keep Houston rented, then pay the separate ISS lease: $400,000 per month of 30 game days. PREPAY TERM offers 1, 3, 6 or 12 months. RENT starts a lease; EXTEND adds time to its current end date. VALID UNTIL shows the deadline and DAYS LEFT shows the remaining time. Each payment resets the rental graph to 100% of all remaining prepaid time, including unused days. Example: 15 days left + a new 30-day payment = 45 days left and a full graph.
ISS renewal is manual. Pay before its deadline. Houston's automatic renewal does not renew ISS. Access is through Houston's OPEN ISS button; RETURN TO HOUSTON leaves the station screen.

HOW TO READ THE GRAPHSELECTRIC POWERAvailable solar power as a percentage. Damage can reduce it.OXYGEN / WATER / FOODLife-support reserves. More people consume them faster. A crew-day is a supply amount for one person for roughly one day; it is not one day for the whole station. Use the accompanying DAYS estimate and leave a reserve for delays.SPARE PARTSMaintenance supplies, also consumed by damage events.ORBITAL PROPELLANTFuel used to raise the station's orbit. The simulation attempts a correction every 30 days and uses 8 tonnes. Insufficient fuel causes lost altitude and condition damage.OVERALL ISS CONDITIONOverall station health. Random small, medium or large micrometeoroid impacts may damage the station and reduce power or supplies.BOARD CAPACITYPeople on board / maximum seven. The starting crew has three people, leaving four places. CREW OCCUPANCY is the percentage of places already used. Houston's astronaut occupancy display refers to people housed at the base, not the number aboard ISS.

AUTOMATIC RESUPPLY
Paying for ISS activates automatic resupply. Choose SOURCE (Florida or Baikonur) and INTERVAL (14, 30 or 45 game days). AUTO NEXT SHIPMENT shows the planned date. Check this date after changing settings; an already planned shipment may retain its date.
Automatic does not mean free: a Florida shipment costs $850,000 and travels for 2 days; Baikonur costs $720,000 and travels for 3 days. The money is charged when the supply ship launches. The departure center must remain rented. SCHEDULED means planned, IN TRANSIT means flying, and DELIVERED means arrived. Only arrival replenishes oxygen, water, food, spare parts and orbital fuel, and improves power and condition.
Weather can postpone departure until a suitable day. Missing funds or a required lease also delay supply. Reserve enough money for both center rent and the shipment, and enough supplies for the interval, travel time and possible delays. Adding crew without shortening a long supply interval can exhaust reserves.

EMERGENCY PLAN · WHAT TO DO
The emergency plan activates automatically if essential supplies have 30 days or less remaining, spare parts fall to 20 or less, fuel to 5 tonnes or less, condition to 35% or less, or power to 30% or less. The station displays WORK / RESEARCH PAUSED and prioritizes survival; the simulation reduces oxygen, water, food and maintenance consumption to 35% of normal.
Pause or slow time and identify the low resource.
Check the ISS deadline, Houston lease, departure center lease and money for the next supply flight.
Check AUTO NEXT SHIPMENT and whether a ship is already IN TRANSIT. A launch alone does not refill the station.
Choose a sustainable supply interval and keep watching reserves while the ship travels. Avoid adding more crew during a shortage.
After recovery above all emergency limits, the emergency status clears automatically. Check fuel and station condition as well as food and water before accelerating time again.

title: WHERE TO CHANGE SETTINGS
text:
WHERE TO CHANGE SETTINGS
Use the screen that owns the setting: crew and maintenance in AIRCRAFT; a soldier's role information and equipment in SOLDIERS; item quantities and trade orders in STORAGE; staff hiring in WORKFORCE; structures in the selected base's construction panel; leases in LOCATIONS. The globe's ALERT panel is for detected threats, and the top bar controls simulation speed.

title: AIRCRAFT & FLIGHT
text:
AIRCRAFT & FLIGHT
INTERCEPTOR: fast, manoeuvrable fighter for UFO interception; its current operational range is 12,000 km. It requires a pilot, fuel, ammunition, maintenance, and time to rearm. A fighter must turn back when its remaining fuel reaches the return-flight reserve.
HOVERCRAFT: transports ground teams and cargo with 25,000 km maximum range. It has pilot and navigator stations and two equipment-pallet spaces.
AWACS: airborne radar platform. Its detection improves with the assigned technician; electronic countermeasures reduce its visibility to UFOs.
Aircraft are managed from AIRCRAFT. Crew assignments, engine and equipment slots, service condition, fuel, ammunition, mission readiness, and operating costs are shown there.

title: PERSONNEL WEAPONS
text:
PERSONNEL WEAPONS
PISTOL is a compact close-range sidearm; RIFLE is a general-purpose weapon; MACHINE GUN supplies sustained fire; ROCKET LAUNCHER attacks at long range with explosive or incendiary rockets. Range, accuracy, weight, and compatible ammunition are listed on each item’s STORAGE detail card.
Weapon magazines and ammunition are separate stock items. Grenades, mines, and flash grenades have different throwing distance and effect radius. Assign weapons and belt items on the soldier equipment screen before deploying.

title: ARMOUR & SOLDIER EQUIPMENT
text:
ARMOUR & SOLDIER EQUIPMENT
Armour is split into helmet, torso, arms, and legs. Each piece protects only its listed body regions. A soldier’s four-slot belt carries small mission items such as magazines and grenades; the backpack carries additional equipment. Medics start with an AID field-aid item.
Role presets include scout, sniper, tank, and medic. They determine a sensible starting weapon and role equipment; all loadout slots remain selectable. Soldier status, training, and hospital assignments are managed from SOLDIERS.

title: BASE FACILITIES
text:
BASE FACILITIES
STORAGE holds 10 equipment pallets per building; the first base starts with two stores and can build more. HANGARS house aircraft; RESEARCH LABS and WORKSHOPS support research and manufacture. POWER PLANTS supply base energy and can currently be built only on the surface. Underground power plants will require a future research unlock. Quarters, soldier barracks, hospital, gym, pilot trainer, radar, satellite facilities, and defence installations provide their named functions.
Buildings are placed from the right-hand BASE construction list. Each entry shows price, footprint, construction time, and energy use. Underground levels add space for eligible facilities. The base grid shows occupied and free cells.

title: CONTACTS, MATERIALS & RESOURCES
text:
CONTACTS, MATERIALS & RESOURCES
UFO contacts can be airborne, landed, or crashed. Globe markers and alert reports show only contacts detected by active radar or satellite sensors; undiscovered grounded incidents still contribute to the strategic alert level. Detection depends on sensor coverage and contact position.
Storage includes personnel and aircraft weapons, ammunition, armour, medical supplies, aircraft components, vehicles, and raw materials such as metals, plastics, glass, electronics, and mineable uranium. Radioactive items carry the radiation symbol. Storage details list current specifications, packed size, and trade prices.
Purchases and sales use national auctions. Cargo aircraft deliver winning lots; sale proceeds arrive on delivery, while inbound goods enter stock only to the extent available warehouse capacity permits.
